title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The ICSP in Zimbabwe focuses on peacebuilding and social cohesion, critical minerals governance, gender justice, and climate change adaptation and resilience. It is implemented by partners CCJP, ZELA, ZPP and WLSA aims to achieve more accountable relationships between communities and government authorities. The objectives of the grant are to support peace and protection, participation and sustainable use of land, and to support civil society to be more resilient so that they can continue to defend human rights and promote accountability. Partners supported rights holders to take action to advance their rights, including community ambassadors and peace committees advocacy through petitions, dialogues, and complaints to raise community concerns and seek solutions by prompting government resonsiveness on issues such as illegal mining and environmental damage; and training and support to community paralegals to accompany cases of GBV. The programme targets communities affected by mining activities in Buhera, Goromonzi and Mutoko; Peacebuilding work focuses on Matobo, Mutasa, Marange districts; and in Chipinge, Mutasa and Marange districts on issues of gender inequality and response to GBV. In 2025, the programme reached 9,270 people directly and 27,623 indirectly. .
